candidates.computation_change_reason: The table distinguishes ambient, effluent, aquatic, domestic-supply, human-health, and TMDL-related criteria. Interpreting whether a measured parameter must be compared to effluent Ce, a derived instream concentration, a human-health criterion, or a TMDL-driven value would change the applicable limit and exceedance determination.

MQL values are listed per pollutant and may be read as method quantitation/reporting thresholds rather than enforceable discharge limits. Treating MQL as a compliance limit versus a detection floor would change whether numeric comparison is applicable and how non-detect or below-quantitation results are classified.

This row supplies a populated effluent concentration Ce (0.2 ug/l) alongside multiple derived and endpoint-specific criteria. Different interpretations of which of these numeric fields is the operative enforceable limit for total mercury would change compliance comparison outcomes.

Ce is blank while other columns contain zeros, finite criteria (1.4, 0.77), and 1E+100 sentinels. Whether a blank Ce means no effluent limit, a limit of zero, or that comparison must use another column affects whether an enforceable numeric limit exists and whether missing/ambiguous evidence should be treated as unresolved.

The segment lists separate rows for dissolved versus total (or total recoverable) forms of the same CAS number. Interpreting which form a reported measurement corresponds to would change which row's limits and MQL apply and which monitoring obligation is implicated.

Paired dissolved/total rows for the same pollutant require a choice of applicable analyte specification. A different mapping from reported parameter names to these rows would change the selected limit and whether monitoring for that form was required.

The (P) notation appears on select parameters and may indicate permit-specific priority, a particular criterion set, or another special status. Reading (P) as triggering a distinct limit or monitoring obligation versus a label only would change applicability for selenium dissolved.

This row states a sulfate-concentration condition (>500 mg/l) for applicability of a separate selenium dissolved criterion set. Whether that condition is met determines which limit row applies, whether conditional monitoring was required, and how to classify periods without results when the condition is unknown.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Multiple finite criteria (5, 20, 5) appear across instream and health columns with zeros elsewhere and 1E+100 sentinels. Interpreting which column governs total recoverable selenium would change the enforceable limit used in exceedance evaluation.

Ce and several derived concentrations are populated with high-precision values while other columns use 1E+100. Different selection among Ce, 2.13*Ce-derived values, or the 9.44030125 instream criterion would yield different applicable limits.

1E+100 appears repeatedly in criterion cells and may be intended to mean no applicable numeric criterion, not applicable, or a placeholder excluding comparison. Treating it as a literal limit versus a non-operative sentinel changes whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable and how missing-evidence cases are classified.
